parties: Continuum Green Energy Limited (investee) | Chubu Electric Power Co., Inc. (investor via affiliate)
headline: Chubu Electric Power invests ₹1,350 crore in Continuum Green Energy via primary and secondary equity
sum: Chubu Electric Power Co., the major Japanese utility, commits ₹1,350 crore (~$145 million) to Continuum Green Energy through a combination of primary share subscription and secondary equity acquisition. The investment is subject to CCI clearance and reflects strategic entry into India's utility-scale renewable energy sector.
implication: Foreign direct investment in renewable energy by a major utility raises FDI sector cap compliance, FEMA Schedule 1 sectoral clearance, and CCI pre-merger review thresholds—a precedent for how Japanese and Asian utilities structure India renewables acquisitions under the foreign shareholding and regulatory gateway model.
detail: Continuum Green Energy, a leading Indian platform for utility-scale wind, solar, and hybrid projects, has secured ₹1,350 crore from Chubu Electric Power Co., Inc. (a major Japanese electric utility) through its affiliate. The transaction comprises both primary subscription (new equity issuance) and secondary acquisition of existing shares. Regulatory approvals, including CCI clearance, remain outstanding. Continuum earlier in 2026 secured $67.5 million from Just Climate, demonstrating active institutional investor interest in India's renewable energy platform space.

framework.ref: Foreign Exchange Management Act, 1999 (FEMA) | Schedule 1, Part A
framework.note: central | FDI into renewable energy: Japanese investor's equity investment requires RBI/FDIR compliance and sectoral cap review for foreign shareholding in renewable power companies
central | Aggregate turnover/group enterprise thresholds trigger CCI pre-merger notification for acquisition of control/material shares in a competing or adjacent power platform

framework.ref: Foreign Direct Investment Policy, 2020 (Government Circular) | Renewable Energy / Power Sector
framework.note: central | Automatic approval route for FDI in renewable energy up to sectoral caps; CCI approval is gateway for control/significant stake
amended | Licensing and regulatory approvals for renewable energy generation projects; affiliate undertaking may require distribution/trading clearances
central | Share subscription, secondary acquisition, and disclosure of substantial shareholding must comply with MCA filing, Board approvals, and shareholder authorization

framework.ref: Sebi (Substantial Acquisition of Shares and Takeovers) Regulations, 2011 | Regulation 3, 4, 5, Schedule
framework.note: amended | If Chubu's aggregate holding (direct + affiliate) crosses 25% threshold post-transaction, mandatory open offer / creeping acquisition exemptions apply

framework.ref: Income Tax Act, 1961 | Chapter XII (Cross-border transactions, TCS on remittance of funds)
framework.note: | Withholding tax on dividend/interest repatriation from India entity to Japan; treaty benefits under India–Japan tax treaty available if conditions met

framework.ref: Ministry of Power / National Portal of India – Investment Clearances
framework.note: | Project-level environmental, land-use, and grid connectivity clearances for underlying wind/solar assets may be required if Chubu exercises operational control

structure.novel: Hybrid structure combining primary equity subscription and secondary share acquisition in a single transaction tranche—enables Japanese utility to gain meaningful operational influence while reducing founder/existing shareholder dilution. Use of affiliate entity for investment permits layered governance and potential future fund consolidation.

triggers.note: Aggregate turnover and group enterprise combined assets likely trigger CCI notification if Chubu gains 'control' (>26% or Board seats) in Continuum or complementary power platform

triggers.law: FEMA / RBI Circular on FDI in Renewable Energy
triggers.note: Automatic approval route applies; however, RBI or FDIR may require documentation of source of funds and beneficial ownership confirmation for Japanese affiliate

If post-transaction shareholding (direct + affiliate) ≥25%, creeping acquisition exemptions or open offer exemptions must be analysed; disclosure requirements to stock exchange (if Continuum is listed) mandatory
